clinician.final_diagnosis: A metal dental crown was removed from the right main bronchus.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old male on hemodialysis presented with persistent cough and recurrent pneumonias. Initial chest radiograph revealed bibasilar infiltrates, atelectasis, and a rounded opaque structure at the right main bronchus. Chest CT confirmed a round dense structure in the right main bronchus likely representing an aspirated foreign body. Bronchoscopy was ordered to visualize and remove the foreign body, supporting the diagnosis of an aspirated metal dental crown causing the patient's symptoms.
